subject: math
title: Comparing Length, Mass and Capacity
seo_title: Grade 1 Comparing Length, Mass and Capacity Worksheets (Free, with Answer Key) | Ontario Math
standard_text: Compare several everyday objects and order them according to length, area, mass, and capacity
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 math worksheets on comparing length, mass and capacity: longer, shorter and taller, measuring with cubes and paper clips with no gaps, heavier and lighter on a balance, which holds more, which covers more, and ordering three objects. 100 picture questions with an answer key, matched to the Ontario curriculum.
key_big: Line up the ends. Lay units end to end: no gaps, no overlaps, all the same.
key_sub: Count the units from one end to the other and say the unit: “6 cubes long”. On a balance the heavier side goes down. Bigger is not always heavier.
body_html:
Longer, shorter and taller

Put two things side by side. Line up one end. Look at the other end. The one that sticks out is longer. The other is shorter. For things that stand up, we say taller and shorter.

Measure with cubes or paper clips

Lay cubes along the object, end to end. Start right at one end. Stop at the other end. Count the cubes. That number is the length. Say the unit too: “6 cubes long”.

Three rules: no gaps, no overlaps and all the units the same.

Heavier and lighter

Put two things on a balance. The heavier side goes down. The lighter side goes up. If the sides are level, they weigh the same.

Holds more and holds less

Fill a jug with cups of water. Use the same cup each time. Count the cups. A container that takes more cups holds more.

Covers more

Cover each shape with squares that are all the same. Count the squares. The shape with more squares covers more.

Order three things

A straw is 10 cubes long. A key is 3 cubes long. A pencil is 7 cubes long. Order them from shortest to longest.

Find the smallest number first: 3, then 7, then 10.

Answer: key, pencil, straw

How many longer?

A pencil is 9 cubes long. A crayon is 5 cubes long. How many cubes longer is the pencil?

9 − 5 = 4. Or count on from 5: 6, 7, 8, 9. That is 4.

Answer: 4 cubes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not lining up the endsStart both objects at the same line
Starting the cubes past the endPut the first cube right at one end
Leaving gaps between cubesPush the cubes together so they touch
Mixing cubes and paper clipsUse one kind of unit all the way
Thinking bigger means heavierUse a balance: the side that goes down is heavier
Thinking longer covers moreCover both shapes with squares and count

faq.q: What measurement do Grade 1 students learn in Ontario math?
faq.a: In the Spatial Sense strand, Grade 1 students learn what can be measured (length, area, mass and capacity) and compare and order everyday objects by these attributes. They also measure length with non-standard units such as cubes and paper clips.

faq.q: What are non-standard units of measurement?
faq.a: Non-standard units are everyday objects of the same size used to measure, like linking cubes, paper clips, craft sticks or cups. They show children that a length is how many equal units fit along an object, before they use rulers.

faq.q: Why must the units touch and be the same size?
faq.a: Gaps and overlaps make the count too small or too big, and units of different sizes make the count meaningless. That is why two people using their own hand spans can get different answers, while two people using the same cubes agree.

faq.q: How can I practise measuring with my Grade 1 child at home?
faq.a: Measure a book or a winter boot with LEGO bricks laid end to end, cover a placemat with sticky notes, count cups of water to fill two containers, and compare two things on a coat hanger balance.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The pencil goes further, so it is longer. The pencil is longer.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The straw goes further, so it is longer. The straw is longer.

items.q: Which is shorter?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The pencil goes further, so it is longer. The nail is shorter.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The marker goes further, so it is longer. The marker is longer.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Both end at the same place. They are the same length.

items.q: Which is shorter?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The strip of paper goes further, so it is longer. The crayon is shorter.

items.q: Which is shorter?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The ribbon goes further, so it is longer. The eraser is shorter.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The craft stick goes further, so it is longer. The craft stick is longer.

items.q: Which is shorter?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The caterpillar goes further, so it is longer. The worm is shorter.

items.q: Which is taller?
items.e: Both stand on the same floor. Look at the tops. The pencil reaches higher, so it is taller. The pencil is taller.

items.q: Which is taller?
items.e: Both stand on the same floor. Look at the tops. The straw reaches higher, so it is taller. The straw is taller.

items.q: Which is shorter?
items.e: Both stand on the same floor. Look at the tops. The craft stick reaches higher, so it is taller. The crayon is shorter.

items.q: Which is taller?
items.e: Both stand on the same floor. The tops are at the same height. They are the same height.

items.q: The ends are not lined up. Which is longer?
items.e: The crayon ends further along, but it starts later. Slide it back so the ends line up. Then the pencil sticks out past it. The pencil is longer.

items.q: The ends are not lined up. Which is longer?
items.e: The straw ends further along, but it starts later. Slide it back so the ends line up. Then the ribbon sticks out past it. The ribbon is longer.

items.q: The ends are not lined up. Which is longer?
items.e: The craft stick ends further along, but it starts later. Slide it back so the ends line up. Then the marker sticks out past it. The marker is longer.

items.q: You want to find the longer pencil. What do you do first?
items.e: Put the pencils side by side. Line up one end. Then look at the other end. The one that sticks out is longer.

items.q: A hockey stick is longer than a ruler. Which is true?
items.e: The hockey stick is longer than the ruler. So the ruler is shorter than the hockey stick. It is the same fact said the other way.

items.q: Chloe and Ethan stand back to back. Chloe’s head is higher. Who is taller?
items.e: Their feet are on the same floor. The higher head belongs to the taller child. Chloe is taller.

items.q: Noah’s scarf is shorter than Lucas’s scarf. Which is true?
items.e: If Noah’s scarf is shorter, then Lucas’s scarf is longer. Lucas’s is longer.

sets.title: Measure with cubes and paper clips

items.q: How many cubes long is the crayon?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the crayon to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4. It is 4 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Count the cubes. How long is the key?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the key to the other: 1, 2, 3. It is 3 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: How many cubes long is the pencil?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the pencil to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. It is 7 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Count the paper clips. How long is the eraser?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the eraser to the other: 1, 2. It is 2 paper clips long. Count the paper clips, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: You measure a crayon with cubes. What do you count?
c: all the cubes in the box
items.e: Lay cubes along the crayon from end to end. Count only the cubes under the crayon. That number is its length.

items.q: How many cubes long is the ribbon?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the ribbon to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. It is 5 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Count the paper clips. How long is the leaf?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the leaf to the other: 1, 2, 3. It is 3 paper clips long. Count the paper clips, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the pencil?
items.e: Yes. The cubes start at one end of the pencil and go to the other end. They touch with no gaps. They are all the same. The pencil is 7 cubes long.

items.q: How many cubes long is the straw?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the straw to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. It is 9 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Count the paper clips. How long is the marker?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the marker to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4. It is 4 paper clips long. Count the paper clips, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Should the cubes touch when you measure?
items.e: Lay the cubes end to end. They must touch, with no gaps and no overlaps.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the crayon?
items.e: No, there are gaps between the paper clips. The gaps are not counted, so the number is too small. Push the paper clips together so they touch.

items.q: How many cubes long is the caterpillar?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the caterpillar to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. It is 6 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Count the paper clips. How long is the strip of paper?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the strip of paper to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. It is 5 paper clips long. Count the paper clips, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the ribbon?
items.e: No, the paper clips overlap. Some lie on top of others, so you count too many. Lay them end to end.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the straw?
items.e: No, the start is wrong. The first cube does not start at the end of the straw. Line up the first one with the end of the straw.

items.q: Count only the cubes under the nail. How long is the nail?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the nail to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. It is 5 cubes long. There are 8 cubes in the row, but only 5 are under the nail. Do not count the extra ones.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the pencil?
items.e: No, the units are mixed. Some are cubes and some are paper clips. A paper clip is longer than a cube, so the count means nothing. Use only one kind of unit.

items.q: Count only the paper clips under the craft stick. How long is the craft stick?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the craft stick to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4. It is 4 paper clips long. There are 6 paper clips in the row, but only 4 are under the craft stick. Do not count the extra ones.

items.q: Maya left gaps between the cubes. She counts 4 cubes. How long is the pencil really?
items.e: The gaps are part of the pencil too, but nobody counted them. So the pencil is more than 4 cubes long. Push the cubes together and count again.

sets.title: Heavier and lighter on a balance

items.q: Which is heavier?
items.e: The heavier side goes down. The book side is down, so the book is heavier.

items.q: Which is heavier?
items.e: The heavier side goes down. The watermelon side is down, so the watermelon is heavier.

items.q: Which is lighter?
items.e: The heavier side goes down and the lighter side goes up. The sponge side is up, so the sponge is lighter.

items.q: Which is lighter?
items.e: The heavier side goes down and the lighter side goes up. The egg side is up, so the egg is lighter.

items.q: On a balance, which side goes down?
items.e: The heavier side goes down. The lighter side goes up.

items.q: The scale is level. Which is true?
items.e: The two sides are level. Neither side goes down. So they weigh the same.

items.q: Which is heavier?
items.e: The heavier side goes down. The brick side is down, so the brick is heavier.

items.q: Which is lighter?
items.e: The heavier side goes down and the lighter side goes up. The pear side is up, so the pear is lighter.

items.q: Which is heavier?
items.e: The heavier side goes down. The stone side is down, so the stone is heavier. The beach ball looks bigger, but bigger is not always heavier.

items.q: Which is heavier?
items.e: The heavier side goes down. The can of beans side is down, so the can of beans is heavier. The pillow looks bigger, but bigger is not always heavier.

items.q: Is a bigger thing always heavier?
items.e: No. A big pillow is lighter than a small can of beans. Put them on a balance to find out.

items.q: The scale is level. How many cubes balance the apple?
items.e: The scale is level, so the cubes weigh the same as the apple. Count the cubes: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. 6 cubes balance the apple.

items.q: The scale is level. How many cubes balance the toy car?
items.e: The scale is level, so the cubes weigh the same as the toy car. Count the cubes: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. 9 cubes balance the toy car.

items.q: The scale is level. How many cubes balance the shoe?
items.e: The scale is level, so the cubes weigh the same as the shoe. Count the cubes: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. 8 cubes balance the shoe.

items.q: Which is true?
c: The orange is lighter than 4 cubes.
The orange weighs the same as 4 cubes.
The orange is heavier than 4 cubes.
items.e: The orange side goes down. The side that goes down is heavier. So the orange is heavier than 4 cubes.

items.q: Which is true?
c: The egg is lighter than 5 cubes.
The egg weighs the same as 5 cubes.
The egg is heavier than 5 cubes.
items.e: The egg side goes up. The side that goes up is lighter. So the egg is lighter than 5 cubes.

items.q: Mateo puts 5 cubes on one side. He puts 3 cubes on the other side. Which side goes down?
items.e: 5 cubes are heavier than 3 cubes. The heavier side goes down: the side with 5 cubes.

items.q: A ball balances 7 cubes. A boot balances 9 cubes. Which is lighter?
items.e: 7 cubes is less than 9 cubes. So the ball is lighter. The boot is heavier.

items.q: Leah holds a book in one hand and an apple in the other. The book pulls her hand down more. Which is heavier?
items.e: The heavier thing pulls your hand down more. So the book is heavier.

items.q: An apple balances 6 cubes. An orange also balances 6 cubes. Which is true?
items.e: Both balance the same number of cubes. So they weigh the same.

items.q: The glasses are the same size. Which has the most water?
items.e: The glasses are the same size, so look for the highest water. Glass A is nearly full. A has the most.

items.q: The glasses are the same size. Which has the least water?
items.e: Look for the lowest water. Glass D is nearly empty. So D has the least.

items.q: Which can hold more water?
items.e: A bathtub is much bigger inside than a cup or a spoon. A bathtub holds more.

items.q: The glasses are the same size. Which has the most water?
items.e: Look for the highest water. Glass C is nearly full. C has the most.

items.q: The glasses are the same size. Which has the least water?
items.e: Look for the lowest water. Glass B is nearly empty. It has less than D. So B has the least.

items.q: Each container is full. Which one holds the most?
items.e: B is the widest and as tall as C. C is tall but very thin. So B holds the most. Tall does not always mean it holds more.

items.q: Each container is full. Which one holds the least?
items.e: C is the thinnest and the shortest. So C holds the least.

items.q: Each container is full. Which one holds the most?
items.e: D is the widest and the tallest. So D holds the most. C is tall, but it is thin.

items.q: Each container is full. Which one holds the least?
items.e: A is the thinnest and the shortest. So A holds the least.

items.q: Owen pours all the cups into the jug. Now the jug is full. How many cups does the jug hold?
items.e: Count the cups: 1, 2, 3. The jug holds 3 cups of water. Do not count the jug.

items.q: Nathan pours all the cups into the jug. Now the jug is full. How many cups does the jug hold?
items.e: Count the cups: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. The jug holds 5 cups of water. Do not count the jug.

items.q: Priya pours all the cups into the jug. Now the jug is full. How many cups does the jug hold?
items.e: Count the cups: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. The jug holds 6 cups of water. Do not count the jug.

items.q: A pot holds 9 cups of water. A bowl holds 4 cups. Which holds more?
items.e: 9 cups is more than 4 cups. So the pot holds more.

items.q: A vase holds 7 cups of water. A kettle holds 10 cups. Which holds less?
items.e: 7 cups is less than 10 cups. So the vase holds less.

items.q: A jug holds 6 cups of water. A pot holds 6 cups too. Which holds more?
items.e: Both hold 6 cups. So they hold the same.

items.q: Emma fills a bottle with water. She pours it all into an empty mug. The mug spills over. Which holds more?
items.e: The water did not all fit in the mug. So the bottle holds more than the mug.

items.q: Aiden pours a full glass into an empty bowl. The bowl is not full yet. Which holds more?
items.e: All the water fit, and there is still room. So the bowl holds more than the glass.

items.q: You fill two jugs with cups of water to compare them. Which cup do you use?
c: a different cup for each jug
a big cup, then a small cup
items.e: Use the same cup each time. Then the counts can be compared. Different cups give counts that do not match.

items.q: Sofia fills a pail with a small cup. Benjamin fills the same pail with a big jug. Who pours more times?
items.e: A small cup holds less each time, so it takes more pours. Sofia pours more times.

items.q: You pour all the water from a tall thin glass into a wide bowl. Is there more water now?
items.e: The water looks lower in the wide bowl, but none was added or spilled. There is the same amount of water.

sets.title: Covers more, ordering and word problems

items.q: Which shape covers more?
items.e: Count the squares. Shape A has 6. Shape B has 4. 6 is more, so shape A covers more.

items.q: How many squares cover this shape?
items.e: Touch each square once as you count: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. 6 squares cover the shape. Do not count the corner square twice.

items.q: Which shape covers more?
items.e: Shape A is longer, but count the squares. Shape A has 8. Shape B has 9. So shape B covers more. Longer does not always mean it covers more.

items.q: Which shape covers less?
items.e: Shape A is long, but it has only 5 squares. Shape B has 7 squares. 5 is less than 7, so shape A covers less.

items.q: How many sticky notes cover the placemat?
items.e: There are 2 rows of 4 notes. Count them all: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. 8 sticky notes cover the placemat. Do not count only the top row.

items.q: Which shape covers more?
items.e: Count the squares. Shape A has 12. Shape B has 12. They look different, but they cover the same.

items.q: Kai covers his book with 8 sticky notes. Zoe covers her book with 10 of the same notes. Whose book covers more?
items.e: 10 notes is more than 8 notes. So Zoe’s book covers more.

items.q: Hana says the longer shape always covers more. Is she right?
items.e: No. A long, thin shape can cover less than a short, wide one. Cover both with the same squares and count.

items.q: Which is the longest?
items.e: All three start at the same line. Look at where each one ends. The straw is the longest. The pencil is in the middle.

items.q: Put them in order from shortest to longest.
items.e: Shortest first. The leaf ends first, then the marker, then the strip of paper. So: leaf, marker, strip of paper. Do not start with the longest.

items.q: Which is the tallest?
items.e: All three stand on the same floor. The straw reaches highest. The straw is the tallest. The pencil is in the middle.

items.q: Which shape covers the most?
items.e: Count the squares. A has 9. B has 10. C has 8. 10 is the most, so shape B covers the most.

items.q: The book is heavier than the apple. The apple is heavier than the feather. Order them from heaviest to lightest.
items.e: The book is heavier than the apple, and the apple is heavier than the feather. Heaviest first: book, apple, feather.

items.q: At the cottage, Olivia fills 3 pails with cups of water. The red pail holds 9 cups. The blue pail holds 6 cups. The yellow pail holds 11 cups. Which holds the least?
items.e: 6 is the smallest number. So the blue pail holds the least. The yellow pail holds the most.

items.q: How many cubes longer is the pencil than the crayon?
items.e: The pencil is 9 cubes long. The crayon is 5 cubes long. Take away the smaller number from the bigger one: 9 − 5 = 4. Or count on from 5 to 9: 6, 7, 8, 9. That is 4 more. Do not add: 9 + 5 = 14 is both together.

items.q: At recess, Jayden builds a tower 9 blocks tall. Arjun’s tower is 4 blocks taller. How tall is Arjun’s tower?
items.e: “4 blocks taller” means add 4. 9 + 4 = 13. It is taller, so the number must be bigger than 9.

items.q: A toy beaver balances 7 cubes. A toy moose balances 12 cubes. How many cubes heavier is the moose?
items.e: Take away the smaller number from the bigger one: 12 − 7 = 5. Or count on from 7 to 12: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. That is 5 more. Do not add: 12 + 7 = 19 is both together.

items.q: At the cottage, a pail holds 9 cups of lake water. Ava pours out 3 cups. How many cups are left?
items.e: Pouring out means take away. 9 − 3 = 6. There are 6 cups left. Do not add: 9 + 3 = 12.

items.q: Amira needs 12 cubes to balance her lunch box. She has put 9 cubes on the scale. How many more cubes does she need?
items.e: Count on from 9 to 12: 10, 11, 12. That is 3. Or 12 − 9 = 3. Check: 9 + 3 = 12.

items.q: A bottle holds 5 cups of water. A jug holds 7 cups. How many cups do they hold together?
items.e: Together means add. 5 + 7 = 12. They hold 12 cups. Do not take away: 7 − 5 = 2 is the difference.
